videos.title: Susan Pwajok on Growing Up on Screen and Surviving Lagos Men | One More Thing
videos.headline: Susan Pwajok on Growing Up on Screen and Surviving Lagos Men | One More Thing
videos.description:
From child star on The Johnsons to Nollywood producer, Suzan Pwajok has spent most of her life in front of a camera, and she's finally telling the full story.

Suzan Pwajok started acting at just four years old, but growing up in the spotlight came with its own challenges. On this episode of One More Thing, she opens up about her journey from child star on The Johnsons to becoming a producer, the reality of going years without acting roles, and why she decided to start creating her own opportunities.

She also shares the story behind her close relationship with her mother, her passion for telling stories about young Northern Nigerian girls, and why she thinks we need to move beyond the pressure to look perfect on social media. Plus, she talks about Binta's, her short film selected for AFRIFF, and what's next for her creative journey.

Watch and enjoy!

videos.title: How Salem King Became Nigeria's Ultimate Creator
videos.headline: How Salem King Became Nigeria's Ultimate Creator
videos.description:
​@salemkinging didn’t set out to become a full-time creator.

The son of ministers, Salem grew up in a home that encouraged curiosity, reading and asking questions. He went on to study Economics at university before entering the world of real estate, where he sold some of the most expensive properties in Nigeria’s most exclusive neighbourhoods.

Then, on the side, he started making content.

What began as a creative experiment quickly turned into something much bigger. His content found an audience, went viral and opened up opportunities he hadn't expected. As his platform grew, Salem began teaching others what he had learnt, sharing his knowledge through a series of classes designed to help aspiring creators build their confidence and find their voice.

Eventually, he made the decision to leave his job and pursue content creation full-time.

Today, Salem King is building the Creatorium franchise and positioning himself at the centre of Nigeria's rapidly evolving creator economy.

In this episode, we talk about his childhood, his journey from Economics to real estate, the moment he discovered the power of content, what going viral really changed, leaving a conventional career behind and what it takes to build a sustainable life as a creator.

videos.headline: RZA on Netflix’s Wu-Tang Documentary, The Secret Album & More (Audio Only) | The Almanac of Rap
videos.description:
What happens when one of hip-hop's most elusive albums becomes the subject of a Netflix documentary? RZA, the visionary producer, filmmaker, and founding architect of the Wu-Tang Clan, joins Donwill to discuss The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable, the new documentary chronicling the extraordinary journey of Once Upon a Time in Shaolin. Created as a single-copy work of art, the album became a multimillion-dollar cultural controversy after its sale to Martin Shkreli, raising questions about artistic ownership, creative freedom, and the value of music in the streaming era. RZA reflects on his relationship with producer Cilvaringz, the persistence that brought him into Wu-Tang's orbit, and the philosophical lessons behind a project whose legacy continues to evolve beyond its creators. The RZA breaks down:

- The story behind Once Upon a Time in Shaolin: Why Wu-Tang created a one-of-a-kind album, the controversy surrounding Martin Shkreli, and the project's continuing legacy.
- Cilvaringz and the philosophy of persistence: How an ambitious young artist earned RZA's attention through preparation, determination, and a willingness to learn.
- Artistic ownership in the streaming era: Why scarcity, direct-to-consumer relationships, and devoted fans can change how independent musicians value their work.
- The Wu-Tang business philosophy: Wu Wear, and the group's extended creative universe helped generate opportunities beyond record sales.
- From Prince Rakeem to filmmaker: RZA's experiences with John Woo, Quentin Tarantino, and other filmmakers shaped his creative evolution and ambitions in cinema.

Now, the next phase for @moniepointmfb  is about driving that impact across the world.

videos.title: Digable Planets on “Jazz Rap”, Winning a Grammy & the Decline of Rap Groups | The Almanac of Rap
videos.headline: Digable Planets on “Jazz Rap”, Winning a Grammy & the Decline of Rap Groups | The Almanac of Rap
videos.description:
Digable Planets helped redefine the possibilities of hip-hop in the early 1990s, blending jazz, funk, political consciousness, and a distinctly cosmic sensibility into a sound that resisted easy categorization. More than three decades later, Ishmael Butler (Butterfly) and Craig Irving (Doodlebug) join Donwill backstage at Brooklyn Bowl to revisit the group's unlikely beginnings, from three artists representing Seattle, Philadelphia, and Maryland to a Grammy-winning collective that made Brooklyn its creative home. They reflect on the success of Reachin' (A New Refutation of Time and Space), the complicated cultural politics of winning a Grammy in hip-hop's early years, and how their revolutionary upbringing informed the music and visual identity of Blowout Comb.  Digable Planets break down:

- The origins of Digable Planets: How three MCs from different cities found one another and built their creative foundation in Brooklyn.
- The making of Blowout Comb: How Black Panther Party newspapers, revolutionary family histories, and live musicians shaped the group's second album.
- The Grammy paradox: Why winning Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group was both a milestone and a complicated achievement in early-'90s hip-hop.
- Why rap groups are disappearing: How social media, individual branding, and changing ideas about community have transformed hip-hop's collaborative culture.
- Beyond the jazz rap label: Why the group resisted genre restrictions, how their music found new life through Snoop Dogg and E-40 samples, and what keeps their catalog relevant across generations.
